subject: Technical Question about Calculated G value

messages.author: 8e259dfec7c9993a
messages.subject: Technical Question about Calculated G value
parts:
Hello,

I would like to know if the {poppr} command automatically scales G with a rarefaction to the minimum sample size, or if there is something else that the user needs to do to obtain a scaled G value. I see that the SE value states that it is scaled based on rarefaction, and I suspect that G is scaled as well. I just want to clarify to make sure because I have not found the answer myself looking through the manual and online tutorials.

Thank you very much!

Caroline

messages.author: d192ec4b1d416345
messages.subject: Re: Technical Question about Calculated G value
parts:
Hello,

The poppr() command does NOT automatically scale G with a rarefaction to the minimum sample size. You can perform this using the diversity_ci() or diversity_boot() functions with the option rarefy = TRUE. An example is laid out in the multilocus genotype vignette: https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/poppr/vignettes/mlg.html#jack-knife-rarefaction

Here's some sample code to extract the rarefied estimate of G with a confidence interval:

library('poppr')
data(monpop)
splitStrata(monpop) <- ~Tree/Year/Symptom
setPop(monpop) <- ~Symptom/Year
mondiv <- diversity_ci(monpop, n = 1000L, rarefy = TRUE, raw = FALSE)

## Samples for rarefaction: 19
mondiv[, c("G.est", "G.ci")]
##       G.est            G.ci
## BB_9  13.88     (8.805, 19)
## FR_9   8.43 (5.232, 12.448)
## BB_10 19.00            <NA>
## FR_10 13.89     (9.256, 19)
## BB_11 19.00            <NA>
## FR_11  8.25  (4.454, 13.37)
## Total 15.52    (10.939, 19)


Hope that helps!

Zhian
